title: Unify networking stage templates and reconcile legacy Terraform state
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Over the last 3 years we accumulated multiple networking Terraform roots and environment-specific templates for staging, perf, and prod. Variations include different VPC module inputs, duplicated NAT/route table resources, and two separate remote state backends (S3 buckets) with slightly different locking settings. This has caused intermittent drift, blocked changes during on-call, and extra cognitive load for platform engineers.

Goals:
- Consolidate networking templates into a single shared module that supports per-environment inputs (vpc_cidr, az_count, private_subnet_suffix).
- Upgrade AWS provider to a supported major version and align Terraform CLI version across CI (lock to 1.5.x).
- Reconcile and migrate legacy remote state into the consolidated backend with explicit state moves (terraform state mv) where needed.
- Add CI acceptance tests, plan checks, and a pre-apply dry-run job for networking changes.

Non-goals:
- Replace existing third-party modules unless they actively block consolidation.
- Tackle application-level iam and kms refactors in this ticket (separate follow-ups).

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Create a v1 of shared module in repo infra/modules/networking-v1 with clear inputs/outputs and examples. Keep feature parity with existing roots.
2) Add a thin wrapper in infra/envs/staging/networking that calls networking-v1 and mirrors current inputs to avoid drift.
3) Upgrade AWS provider in a feature branch: bump provider constraint to ">= 4.0" and run terraform init -upgrade in a sandbox workspace. Audit provider changelog for any resource attribute changes and map them in a provider-upgrade-migration.md doc.
4) For each legacy root (staging-old, perf-old): plan a state migration path:
   - run terraform state list to inventory resources
   - run terraform state mv to move resources from legacy root into new consolidated root addresses where module structure differs
   - record explicit state moves in a migration plan file to make changes auditable
5) Use a dedicated temporary remote state bucket prefix (s3://redwood-infra-migrations/<ticket>) and locking to perform the moves safely.
6) Add acceptance tests to CI: create the VPC with small-sized resources in the test account, validate routes/security groups, then destroy. Use terratest or a small kube job that validates network reachability.
7) Rollout: apply consolidated staging first, validate traffic and downstream tests, then schedule perf and prod migrations during low-traffic windows with runbooks and rollback steps.

Testing and validation:
- Plan-only runs on forks and an internal validation workspace.
- Dry-run migration in a mirror sandbox account to validate all state moves succeed.
- Post-migration checks: resource counts, attached routes, CIDR overlap checks, and smoke tests for downstream services.

Rollback strategy:
- Keep original remote state snapshot (S3 versioning + state export) before any state move.
- If migration fails, restore the snapshot and run terraform apply on the legacy root to return to the previous state.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: state move mistakes leading to resource orphaning. Mitigation: small incremental moves, two engineers required to approve each move, perform in the sandbox first.
- Risk: provider upgrade changes resource schemas. Mitigation: audit changelog, run plan and compare diffs, pin module versions, and open targeted PRs to address attribute changes.
- Risk: downtime for dependent services during prod migration. Mitigation: schedule during maintenance window, communicate with owners, and leverage rollback snapshot.

Artifacts / Links:
- RFC / Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Network+Consolidation+RFC
- Migration runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ExampleMigrationRunbook
- Sandbox PR for provider bump: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1248
- Example terraform commands: "terraform init -backend-config=... && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan"

Acceptance criteria:
- Shared networking module merged and consumed by infra/envs/staging/networking wrapper.
- AWS provider constraint updated and validated in a sandbox workspace with zero destructive changes after plans.
- Legacy remote state for 'staging-old' successfully migrated into consolidated root with a documented sequence of terraform state mv steps and S3 state snapshots.
- CI tests added to run terraform plan and a lightweight acceptance test in the staging account.

Next steps / tasks:
- [ ] Create module scaffold and initial unit examples (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Prepare provider upgrade PR and smoke-run in sandbox (owner: Miguel + Ops)
- [ ] Draft migration plan for staging-old and perform sandbox migration (owner: Asha + Miguel)
- [ ] Add CI acceptance job and Terratest example (owner: SRE team)

Notes from recent sync:
- PM feedback: avoid changing prod networking naming; prefer aliasing new module inputs to maintain resource addresses where possible.
- Security review: request raised with secops; expect a short review for provider upgrade and S3 bucket ACL changes.
comments: 2025-02-06: Ticket created after triage with infra team. Initial backlog grooming done; scoped to staging-first approach.
2025-02-08: Miguel pushed module scaffold branch and opened PR #1248. Set up a sandbox workspace for provider upgrade tests.
2025-02-10: Found two legacy state buckets with differing locking settings; creating a replicated temporary bucket for migrations to avoid cross-region locking issues.
2025-02-11: Security asked to review S3 bucket policy changes; secops requested explicit encryption and deny-public-access — we will apply that in the migration prep.

2025-02-12: Ran a dry-run state move in sandbox for a single subnet resource; move succeeded and we documented the exact terraform state mv sequence. Next: schedule a paired run for full staging migration.
